about: One brief per type of deliverable: what a good one looks like. Added to the mission of every kit template (backend/roles.py · deliverable_brief). Instructions for the agent are in English; the work's brief tells it which language to write in.

structure: subject line (« Objet : … ») that says what the letter is about in under 12 words
salutation adapted to the addressee (« Madame, Monsieur, » when unknown)
first paragraph: why we write, referring to the earlier exchange or document by its date or number
body: the facts and what we propose or ask, one idea per paragraph
the expected next step, with who does what and by when
formal closing and signature block (name, function, organisation) left for the person to complete
letter.length: A letter fits on one page (150-350 words); an e-mail 80-200 words. Shorter is better when nothing is lost.
letter.sources: Every reference, number, amount, date and name comes from the attached documents or the person's request; quote numbers and amounts exactly as written there. Never invent a commitment, a deadline or a discount.
letter.verify: List the addressee's exact name and title, every amount and date, and any commitment the letter makes on behalf of the organisation.

structure: title and one line « for whom / for what decision »
the answer or recommendation first, in 3 to 5 lines
key points grouped by theme, each with the document it comes from
figures, dates and commitments that matter, exactly as written
what the documents leave open or contradict (both versions shown)
memo.length: One to two pages (400-900 words). A reader in a hurry must get the essential from the first five lines.
memo.sources: Name the source document of each important point « (source : nom du document) ». Nothing that is not in the documents; when two documents disagree, show both.
memo.verify: List the figures and dates to check against the originals, and the points where the documents disagree or are silent.

structure: title, scope and period covered
summary in five lines: the findings and what they mean
context and method (which documents were used, what was compared)
findings, one section each, with the figures and their source
risks, limits and open questions
recommendations or options, each with its consequence
report.length: Two to five pages. Tables for any comparison of more than three figures.
report.sources: Every figure is quoted from a named document, with its period; a computed figure (sum, ratio, variation) shows how it was computed from the source figures. No external figure, benchmark or statistic that is not in the documents.
report.verify: List every computed figure with its calculation, the assumptions made, and the conclusions a human must confirm before the report goes out.

structure: objective and audience in two lines
the steps or modules in order, each with its owner, duration or date, and deliverable
a summary table (step, who, when, done-when)
resources, constraints and dependencies
risks and what to do if they occur
plan.length: One to three pages; the summary table must fit on one page.
plan.sources: Dates, durations, people and budgets come from the documents or the request; when one is missing, write « [à définir] » rather than a plausible value.
plan.verify: List every date and owner that was not given explicitly, and every dependency that could move the schedule.

structure: one header row with explicit column names (unit in the name: « Montant (CHF) »)
one row per item, in a meaningful order (date, amount or priority)
a column « Source » naming the document and page or line each row comes from
a column « À vérifier » (oui/non or a short reason) when the item is uncertain
total or subtotal rows labelled as such, at the end
table.length: As many rows as the documents justify, no padding rows; at most 12 columns.
table.sources: Every cell value is copied from a named document; a computed cell (total, difference) is labelled as computed in its row. Never fill a missing value with an estimate: leave it empty and mark the row « À vérifier ».
table.verify: In your message, say how many rows are marked « À vérifier », which totals were computed, and what was left empty.

structure: title and when to use the checklist
the items grouped by phase or by owner, each as a checkbox « - [ ] »
for each item: who, by when, and the proof that it is done
items that depend on a decision still to take, marked as such
checklist.length: One to two pages; 10 to 40 items. Each item starts with a verb.
checklist.sources: Items come from the documents (procedures, contracts, regulations given) and the request; an item added from general good practice is marked « (bonne pratique) ».
checklist.verify: List the items added from good practice rather than from the documents, and the owners or deadlines that are assumed.

structure: meeting name, date, place, participants and excused (as given)
agenda items in order, each with the points discussed in neutral wording
decisions taken, numbered, each in one sentence
action table: action, owner, deadline
next meeting, if known
minutes.length: One to three pages. Neutral, factual, past tense; no opinion attributed to a person unless the notes attribute it.
minutes.sources: Only what the notes or recording transcript say; a name, a decision or a deadline that is not in the notes is not added.
minutes.verify: List the decisions and deadlines whose wording must be confirmed by the chair, and any participant or owner the notes leave unclear.

structure: a hook in one sentence
the message in two to four short paragraphs or bullet points
the call to action (what the reader should do, where)
two alternative versions of the hook, clearly marked
short.length: Within the channel's limit given in the request (default 120-250 words); no hashtags or emojis unless the team's charter asks for them.
short.sources: Facts, dates, prices and names come from the documents; no claim that cannot be proven from them (« le meilleur », « n°1 »).
short.verify: List every fact or figure the text states, the claims a human must be able to prove, and the people or partners named (consent to be named).

structure: purpose, scope and who it is for
prerequisites (access, documents, tools)
numbered steps, one action per step, with the expected result
exceptions and what to do when something goes wrong
who owns the procedure and when it is reviewed
procedure.length: One to three pages; steps short enough to follow while doing them.
procedure.sources: Steps come from the documents and the request; a step added from good practice is marked « (bonne pratique) ». Tool names and screens are named as the documents name them.
procedure.verify: List the steps that were inferred rather than read, and the owners and review date to confirm.

structure: document reviewed (name, version or date), purpose of the review
summary: the three to five points that matter most
a table of the clauses or passages reviewed: reference, what it says (quoted), issue, suggested wording or question
points missing from the document
questions for the specialist or the counterparty
review.length: Two to four pages; quote the exact passage for every issue raised.
review.sources: Quote the document word for word with its article or page; a reference to a law or a standard is given only when the documents provided name it. This is a preparation for a specialist, never a legal or tax opinion.
review.verify: List each issue a qualified person must confirm, and every legal or regulatory reference that must be checked in the current text.
